Python cells inside the divs Quarto provides: callouts, tabsets, and page
columns, each on its own and inside a `.panzoom` div, as [Divs in
R](p-divs.html) does for R cells and images. lightbox is off, so clicking a plot
panzoom leaves alone does nothing.

A plot on a tab not selected, or in a collapsed callout, opens once the reader
selects the tab or expands the callout.

Each case shows its source above the plot: Jupyter leaves `panzoom:` out of the
echoed code of a cell.

The plots are drawn with these helpers:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def wave(k=1):
    x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
    col = plt.cm.Dark2(k - 1)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
    ax.fill_between(x, np.sin(k * x), color=col, alpha=0.35, linewidth=0)
    ax.plot(x, np.sin(k * x), color=col, linewidth=2)
    ax.set(title=f"Wave {k}", xlabel="x", ylabel="sin(kx)")
    plt.show()


# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
def collage(n=12, height=0.8, width=8):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n, figsize=(width, height), layout="constrained")
    for i, ax in enumerate(axes):
        ax.plot(np.cumsum(rng.normal(size=200)), color=plt.cm.viridis(i / n))
        ax.set_title(f"Panel {i + 1}", fontsize=5)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=4)
    plt.show()
```

## Plot in a callout {#c1 expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with `panzoom: true` in a callout. It opens in panzoom.

````markdown {.code-overflow-wrap .cell-code}
::: {.callout-note title="A note with a plot"}
```{{python}}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve, shaded between the curve and y = 0"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 1: y = sin(x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(1)
```
:::
````

::: {.callout-note title="A note with a plot"}
```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve, shaded between the curve and y = 0"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 1: y = sin(x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(1)
```
:::

## Callout in a `.panzoom` div {#c2 expect-open="panzoom"}

A callout with a cell that has no `panzoom` option, inside a `.panzoom` div. The
div marks every figure in it, so the plot opens in panzoom.

````markdown {.code-overflow-wrap .cell-code}
::: {.panzoom}
::: {.callout-tip title="A tip with a plot"}
```{{python}}
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve, shaded between the curve and y = 0"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(2)
```
:::
:::
````

::: {.panzoom}
::::: {.callout-tip title="A tip with a plot"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve, shaded between the curve and y = 0"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(2)
```
:::::
:::

## Collage across the screen {#c7 expect-fit="height"}

An 8 × 0.8 inch collage in a `.column-screen` div, so it spans the window. It is
a strip, so it opens in panzoom at screen height.

````markdown {.code-overflow-wrap .cell-code}
::: {.column-screen}
```{{python}}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "An 8 × 0.8 inch collage of 12 random walks."

collage(n=12)
```
:::
````

::: {.column-screen}
```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A row of 12 small line plots of random walks, each in its own color
#| fig-cap: "An 8 × 0.8 inch collage of 12 random walks."

collage(n=12)
```
:::
